rootCause.explanation: Repository name/description searches pass user substrings to builder.Like. Its terminal-percent wildcard handling does not preserve a trailing literal percent as a substring match.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A saved branch containing an allowed percent sign is found by an ordinary substring or full name but disappears for a matching substring ending in percent.

sourceBugs.name: Branch search loses matching literal-percent substrings

reproductionPaths.expected: Branch search must retain the existing qa/hash#percent% result for matching substrings such as percent% and hash#percent%, as it does for percent and the complete saved name.
reproductionPaths.actual: Searching percent finds qa/hash#percent%; percent% and hash#percent% show no matching branch. Searching the complete qa/hash#percent% finds it again.
reproSteps: In eval/harbor-handbook, create a branch from main named qa/hash#percent% using the normal branch-creation control.
Open the repository Branches page and search for percent. Confirm the saved branch appears below the default branch.
Replace the query with percent% and submit. Observe that the matching branch disappears.
Search hash#percent% and observe the same missing result. Search the complete qa/hash#percent% and confirm the branch reappears.

logicalBugs.explanation: Empty uploads become 1024 NUL bytes.

rootCause.explanation: UploadFileToServer allocates a 1024-byte probe and slices it only when n>0; NewUpload writes the entire unsliced zero buffer for an empty file.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A genuine zero-byte text upload is stored and committed as a 1024-byte binary file; the downloaded bytes change, as well as its displayed size and editability.

sourceBugs.name: Uploading an empty file commits 1024 NUL bytes

reproductionPaths.expected: Preserve uploaded file contents exactly. A zero-byte file must remain zero bytes after commit and download, as a blank file created through New File does.
reproductionPaths.actual: The upload card shows 0 B, but after commit the file is 1.0 KiB and binary with copy/edit unavailable. Download yields exactly 1024 NUL bytes. A blank editor-created file on the same branch remains 0 B plaintext.
reproSteps: Sign in to eval/harbor-handbook and create a disposable branch from main.
Prepare a genuinely empty .txt file and confirm its local size is 0 bytes. Use Add File → Upload File and confirm its upload card shows 0 B.
Commit the upload, open the resulting file, and click Download. Inspect the downloaded file: it contains 1024 bytes, each NUL.
As a control on the same branch, use Add File → New File to create another .txt with a blank editor. Commit and confirm the empty-file dialog; it remains 0 B plaintext.

guidance.scope: Credit persistent upload-byte corruption, confirmed by download. An incorrect size label alone is insufficient for this severity-3 reference.

matchingGuidance.scope: Credit persistent upload-byte corruption, confirmed by download. An incorrect size label alone is insufficient for this severity-3 reference.

logicalBugs.explanation: Upstream merge references link to nonexistent fork issues.

rootCause.explanation: Commit message issue-reference rendering uses the current repository context, with no upstream origin resolution for a synced upstream merge commit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After syncing a fork with its upstream repository, the fork's commit history renders the upstream merge commit's #3 pull request reference as a link under the fork, where that issue does not exist. The link opens a 404 instead of the actual upstream pull request.

reproductionPaths.expected: A pull request number embedded in an upstream merge commit should link to the pull request in the upstream repository, eval/D-from-template/pulls/3, or otherwise avoid a broken link in the fork's history.

reproSteps: Sign in using the fixture accounts. Create a public repository as eval and fork it as alex.
As alex, create a contribution branch in the fork, add a file, and open a pull request against the upstream main branch.
As eval, merge that pull request using the default merge-commit message.
Sync the fork’s main branch with the upstream main branch.
Open the fork’s Commits page and click the #N pull-request reference in the generated merge-commit subject.
Observe that the link targets an issue in the fork and returns 404, while the upstream /eval/<upstream-repository>/pulls/N page exists and returns 200.

logicalBugs.explanation: Reverse comparison calls an ancestor branch equal to its descendant.

rootCause.explanation: PrepareCompareDiff marks IsNothingToCompare when head equals MergeBase, using merge-base comparison semantics to display an equality claim even when the base has additional commits.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Reversing the two repository branches makes the read-only Compare commits view claim they are equal, despite the opposite direction showing one commit and a file diff; this persisted after refresh and a repeat reversal.

sourceBugs.name: Reverse comparison labels distinct branches as equal

reproductionPaths.expected: With docs/release-owners as the base and main as the compare branch, the read-only comparison should accurately indicate that main has no commits ahead of docs/release-owners, not say the branches are equal.
reproductionPaths.actual: At /admin/harbor-handbook/compare/docs/release-owners..main, the visible Compare commits page says “These branches are equal.” In the opposite direction, main versus docs/release-owners showed 1 commit and a docs/releases.md diff. Refreshing and reversing again reproduced the equality message.
reproSteps: Use the supplied signed-in administrator session (authenticated via saved session; no environment-variable credentials used) and open /admin/harbor-handbook.
Open the Code tab, select docs/release-owners in the branch selector, and click the adjacent comparison control.

On the comparison preview, use the comparison-type control to open the read-only Compare commits view at /admin/harbor-handbook/compare/main..docs/release-owners. Confirm it shows 1 commit and a docs/releases.md diff.
Click the “Switch head and base” arrow. The resulting page at /admin/harbor-handbook/compare/docs/release-owners..main displays “These branches are equal.”
Refresh and repeat the reversal to confirm the message persists. Do not submit a pull request.

logicalBugs.explanation: Exact code search drops leading hyphens.

rootCause.explanation: Grep builds the -e pattern using strings.TrimLeft(search,"-") even though -e already safely separates the pattern from options.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Exact searches for '-Harbor' or '--Harbor' return lines containing 'Harbor' without the required hyphens.

sourceBugs.name: Exact code search silently removes leading hyphens

reproductionPaths.expected: Exact search should preserve the entire search term and only return lines containing '-Harbor' (or '--Harbor' respectively). These seeded README lines should not match.
reproductionPaths.actual: Searching '-Harbor' returns README lines '# Harbor engineering handbook' and 'Welcome to Harbor...' even though neither contains '-Harbor'. Searching '--Harbor' produces the same false matches. Source modules/git/grep.go strips all leading hyphens with strings.TrimLeft(search, "-") before passing the query as an -e value.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open /eval/harbor-handbook.
Enter '-Harbor' in Search code and submit.
Keep Search type set to Exact (its description says it only includes results matching the exact search term).
Observe README results containing Harbor with no preceding hyphen.
Repeat with '--Harbor' and observe the same false matches.

guidance.rootCause: SearchModeExact reaches GrepModeExact, whose git grep pattern removes all leading hyphens with strings.TrimLeft(search, "-"). The original command wrapper rejects leading hyphens in dynamic option values.

matchingGuidance.rootCause: SearchModeExact reaches GrepModeExact, whose git grep pattern removes all leading hyphens with strings.TrimLeft(search, "-"). The original command wrapper rejects leading hyphens in dynamic option values.

Read the visible XML channel <link>: /eval/harbor-handbook/branch/main.

guidance.scope: Branch-list RSS feed to the branch directory page. The README-toolbar RSS feed to a file page has its own accepted reference.
guidance.rootCause: Verified in go-gitea/gitea tag v1.24.7: routers/web/feed/branch.go, ShowBranchFeed, constructs the channel href as repo.HTMLURL() + "/" + ctx.Repo.RefTypeNameSubURL(). logicalBugs.explanation: Branch/tag names and ref lifetime changes reuse stale commit counts.

rootCause.explanation: GetCommitsCount keys ref caches by RefFullName.ShortName plus a shared ref marker, omitting ref type and tip SHA. Same-named tag/branch collide and ref updates/recreation/rename retain cached history counts.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After the longer same-named branch history has been visited, a tag's Code and History views show the branch's cached commit count even though the tag points to one commit, exposing a nonexistent empty history page.

reproductionPaths.expected: The tag's commit count and pagination should describe the tag's own history. A one-commit tag should show one commit and no second page, regardless of a same-named branch.
reproductionPaths.actual: After visiting the longer branch history first to populate the count cache, opening the unchanged one-commit tag shows 51 Commits. Its History page has the single tag commit, but still reports 51; clicking Next opens an empty second page. Reloading preserves the incorrect count.

Open /eval/harbor-handbook/src/tag/qa/code-renamed. Its file tree is the initial three-file snapshot, while the statistics link says 51 Commits.
Open /eval/harbor-handbook/commits/tag/qa/code-renamed. Observe the 51 Commits heading with only the initial 4ff25d14a0 row.

In the fork, open the branch and click Sync fork, then confirm.

reproductionPaths.explanation: With a file open in the editor, if the file is renamed or deleted in another tab, clicking Preview Changes shows an 'Error 500' banner and an empty preview. The preview request still uses the original path and treats the missing file as a server error, while committing from the same editor shows a readable message that the file no longer exists.

sourceBugs.name: Preview Changes returns Error 500 after the edited file is renamed or deleted elsewhere

reproductionPaths.expected: Preview Changes on a file that has since been renamed or deleted shows the same readable message as committing does ('The file being edited, "<name>", no longer exists in this repository.'), not a server error.
reproductionPaths.actual: After qa-collab-alex.txt was renamed in another tab, clicking Preview Changes in the original editor showed a red 'Error 500 when calling /eval/harbor-handbook/_preview/qa-collab-alex-recovery/qa-collab-alex.txt' banner and an empty preview panel. Deleting the file instead of renaming it gave the same result.
reproSteps: Open a file's Edit File page in two tabs.
In the second tab, rename (or delete) the file and commit.
In the first tab, change the content and click Preview Changes.
Check what the preview shows.

logicalBugs.explanation: Code search silently truncates at 50 matching files.

rootCause.explanation: Grep defaults MaxResultLimit to 50 and cancels once reached, but result presentation does not expose a truncation indicator.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Without a code indexer, repository code search uses git grep and only returns the first 50 matching files, but the results page doesn't say the list was truncated: the pager ends at the 50th file as if those were all the matches.

sourceBugs.name: Repository code search stops at 50 matching files without saying the results were cut off

reproductionPaths.expected: When code search stops at its result limit, the page says the results were cut off, so the user knows more files match.
reproductionPaths.actual: A search matching 65 files showed results 001–020, 021–040 and 041–050 across three pages, then Next and Last were disabled; files 051–065 couldn't be reached, and no message said a limit had been hit.
reproSteps: In a repository with no code indexer, add more than 50 files containing the same unique word.
Search the repository's code for that word.
Page to the end of the results.
Check whether all matching files are reachable or a message says the results were truncated.

logicalBugs.explanation: Backspace merges a parent directory while a filename selection exists.

rootCause.explanation: The keydown branch tests selectionStart==0 but never checks selectionEnd; a selection starting at zero incorrectly triggers moving the last folder into the filename.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the file editor's path field, Backspace at the very start of the name intentionally pulls the last folder back into the name (the inverse of typing '/'). But the check only looks at where the selection starts, so selecting the whole name and pressing Backspace also triggers it: the selected text isn't deleted, the parent folder is prefixed onto it, and the folder disappears from the path. The same happens in the Upload File directory field.

sourceBugs.name: Backspace on a selected file name in the editor merges the parent folder into the name instead of clearing it

reproductionPaths.expected: With the whole file name selected, Backspace deletes the selection and leaves the folder path unchanged, so a new name can be typed.
reproductionPaths.actual: Editing qa-paths-fixtures/source/nested/destination/recovered.md, selecting the whole name and pressing Backspace changed the name to destinationrecovered.md and removed destination from the breadcrumb, leaving qa-paths-fixtures/source/nested.
reproSteps: Open a file inside a folder and click Edit File.
Click in the file name field, press Ctrl+A to select the whole name, then press Backspace.
Check whether the name was cleared or the parent folder was merged into it and removed from the path.

logicalBugs.explanation: Cancel after a failed rename opens the attempted destination.

rootCause.explanation: The error form renders cancellation from the submitted tree_path instead of retaining the original existing source path, producing a 404 destination.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the file editor, if renaming or moving a file is rejected (for example because part of the new path is an existing file), the editor's Cancel link then points at the rejected new path instead of the original file, so clicking Cancel opens a 404. The error page renders with the attempted path as the current file path.

sourceBugs.name: Cancel after a rejected file rename opens the attempted path and a 404

reproductionPaths.expected: Cancel after a rejected rename returns to the original file, which still exists unchanged.
reproductionPaths.actual: Editing qa-paths-fixtures/source/nested/up-one.md and renaming it to destination/occupied.md/child.md was rejected because occupied.md is a file. Clicking Cancel then opened qa-paths-fixtures/source/nested/destination/occupied.md/child.md, which showed '404 Not Found'.
reproSteps: In a folder that contains a file (for example occupied.md), open another file's editor.
Change its name to a path that goes through that file (for example occupied.md/child.md) and commit; the change is rejected.
On the error page, click Cancel next to the file name.
Check whether you're taken back to the original file or to a 404.

logicalBugs.explanation: Apply Patch existing-branch errors render the file editor and crash.

rootCause.explanation: The branch-exists error path renders tplEditFile rather than tplPatchFile, without the file-editor template data required by that unrelated page.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a repository's Apply Patch page, choosing 'Create a new branch' with the name of a branch that already exists correctly shows 'Branch "<name>" already exists in this repository.', but the rest of the page is a 500 Internal Server Error (a template render failure) instead of the Apply Patch form, so the patch and commit message are lost. The handler renders the file editor's template for this error instead of the patch template.

sourceBugs.name: Apply Patch to a new branch whose name already exists shows a full-page 500

reproductionPaths.expected: The duplicate-branch message is shown on the Apply Patch form, with the patch and commit fields kept, so the user can pick another branch name.
reproductionPaths.actual: Submitting a patch to the new branch name qa-patch-20260718-a, which already existed, showed 'Branch "qa-patch-20260718-a" already exists in this repository.' above a 500 Internal Server Error with template-render error text; the Apply Patch form, patch and commit summary were gone.
reproSteps: In a repository with a branch named, for example, existing-branch, choose Add File > Apply Patch.
Paste a valid patch, choose 'Create a new branch for this commit', enter existing-branch as the new branch name, and click Propose file change.
Check whether the Apply Patch form is shown with the error, or a 500 page.

logicalBugs.explanation: An invalid new-branch name blocks a direct commit choice.

rootCause.explanation: The shared form still binds/validates NewBranchName from the inactive branch field; switching CommitChoice back does not clear or disable that field, so its GitRefName validation still rejects the form.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the file editor (also Delete and Upload), after typing an invalid name under 'Create a new branch for this commit' and then switching to 'Commit directly to the branch', the hidden new-branch name is still validated, so Commit Changes is refused with 'New branch name must be a well-formed Git reference name.' even though no new branch will be created.

sourceBugs.name: An invalid new-branch name blocks committing directly after switching back to the current branch

reproductionPaths.expected: With 'Commit directly' selected, the unused new-branch name is ignored and the commit goes through to the current branch.
reproductionPaths.actual: After entering qa-edit-boundary-invalid.lock as the new branch name, getting the reference-name error, and switching to 'Commit directly' (which hides the field and relabels the button Commit Changes), clicking Commit Changes kept the editor open with 'New branch name must be a well-formed Git reference name.' and the file wasn't saved.
reproSteps: Edit or create a file, choose 'Create a new branch for this commit', and enter an invalid branch name such as bad..name.
Submit and see the reference-name error.
Switch to 'Commit directly to the branch' and click Commit Changes.
Check whether the commit is saved or the new-branch-name error appears again.

logicalBugs.explanation: Same-named upload entries silently replace one another.

rootCause.explanation: UploadRepoFiles stages each upload using its original name as the index path without rejecting duplicate target paths, so the final blob wins.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On Upload File, two files with the same name can be added to the same upload. Both are listed as uploaded and Commit Changes succeeds without any warning, but only one of them is committed; the other's content is silently discarded.

sourceBugs.name: Uploading two files with the same name silently commits only one

reproductionPaths.expected: Uploading two files with the same name is rejected or the conflict is resolved clearly before committing, instead of silently losing one file.
reproductionPaths.actual: Both same-named files appeared in the upload area and Commit Changes returned to the repository with no conflict message. Only one file was committed, holding the first file's content; the second file's content was lost.
reproSteps: Open Add File > Upload File on a test branch.
Add a text file, then add a second text file with the same name but different content.
Click Commit Changes.
Open the committed file and check whose content it holds, and whether any warning appeared.

logicalBugs.explanation: Syncing an ahead-only fork reports a server failure.

rootCause.explanation: GetBranchDivergingInfo uses branch UpdatedUnix timestamps when its fast path cannot calculate divergence, so a newly created upstream branch at an older common commit is incorrectly marked as having new commits. MergeUpstream then attempts a merge instead of returning up-to-date.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a fork branch that has its own commits but nothing new upstream (the upstream branch was created later at the common base), the banner wrongly says upstream has new changes, and confirming Sync fork shows "server error: 500".

sourceBugs.name: Sync fork on a branch that is only ahead of upstream fails with a server error

reproductionPaths.expected: A fork branch that is only ahead of upstream shows no sync banner, or syncing it reports that there's nothing to update.
reproductionPaths.actual: The banner said the base branch had new changes. Confirming Sync fork showed a red "server error: 500"; the fork's commit was kept and the banner stayed.
reproSteps: Fork a repository and, in the fork, create a new branch from main and commit a change to it.
In the upstream repository, create a branch with the same name from main without new commits.
Open the fork's branch and check the sync banner.
Click Sync fork and confirm.

logicalBugs.explanation: A zero-based line range raises a JavaScript error.

rootCause.explanation: Line selection uses one-based line indexes from the hash without rejecting zero before indexing line DOM elements.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Opening a source file with a zero-based line fragment such as #L0-L3 displays a JavaScript error banner.

sourceBugs.name: Zero-based line range shows a JavaScript error banner

reproductionPaths.expected: An unsupported zero-based line range is ignored or handled without an unhandled JavaScript error banner.
reproductionPaths.actual: A red banner reading "JavaScript error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'closest')" appears above the repository.
reproSteps: Open a repository file such as README.md in View Source.
Replace the URL fragment with #L0-L3 and navigate to it.
Observe the red JavaScript error banner above the repository.

logicalBugs.explanation: Apply Patch validation leaves its submit control disabled.

rootCause.explanation: After the validation response, editor dirty tracking treats the restored patch as its clean baseline and watches only fields outside .commit-form-wrapper. Branch and message corrections are excluded, so only changing patch text enables commit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When Apply Patch rejects an invalid new-branch name (for example one with consecutive dots), the page reloads with the patch and the error, but the Propose file change / Commit Changes button stays disabled after the name is corrected. Only editing the patch text itself re-enables it.

sourceBugs.name: After Apply Patch rejects an invalid branch name, correcting it leaves the submit button disabled

reproductionPaths.expected: After correcting the branch name on the reloaded Apply Patch page, the submit button is enabled so the patch can be applied.
reproductionPaths.actual: After the rejection, correcting the branch name, changing the commit message or switching to committing directly left the button disabled; it was enabled again only after changing the patch text.
reproSteps: Open Apply Patch, paste a valid patch, choose to create a new branch, and enter an invalid name such as qa..bad.
Submit and wait for the error.
Correct the branch name to a valid one.
Check whether the submit button becomes enabled.

logicalBugs.explanation: Filtered commit diffs keep the unfiltered file tree.

rootCause.explanation: The diff file tree uses the commit full changed-file summary while only the body is filtered; it renders links to absent body anchors without a filter indicator or navigation behavior.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Opening a commit's diff filtered to one file (for example History > View changes to this file in this commit, which adds ?files=<path>) shows only that file's diff, but the changed-file tree and the "N changed files" header still list every file in the commit, with nothing indicating the view is filtered or how to see the rest.

sourceBugs.name: Filtered commit diff lists every changed file without showing that it's filtered

reproductionPaths.expected: A filtered commit diff makes clear that it's filtered, for example by listing only the shown files or marking the others and offering a way to show all changes.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the diff filtered to one file, the tree still listed all three changed files and the header said 3 changed files, but only one diff was shown, with no filter indicator.
reproSteps: Open a file's History and choose View changes to this file in this commit for a commit that changed several files.
Compare the file tree and the changed-files count with the diffs shown on the page.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In a commit diff filtered to one file (?files=<path>), clicking another file in the changed-file tree does nothing: the link points to a diff that isn't on the page, so the view stays on the filtered file with no navigation or message.

sourceBugs.name: Clicking a file that isn't in a filtered commit diff does nothing

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking a file in the tree opens or loads that file's diff (for example by leaving the filtered view), or the file isn't offered as a link.
reproductionPaths.actual: Clicking a file that wasn't in the filtered diff only changed the URL fragment; nothing scrolled, loaded or explained why, and the page stayed on the filtered file.

In the changed-file tree, click a different file from that commit.
Check whether its diff opens.
